name: indexbyte
algorithm: Find the first 0xFF byte of a buffer of 7-bit bytes, the needle planted within the last 64 bytes and removed after each search; reps searches (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: no integer arithmetic to wrap in the kernel

notes: GB/s counts size * reps bytes; each search reads all but at most 64 bytes of the buffer. The fill (one arithmetic pass) and its first-touch page faults are timed by each variant's baseline (reps 0) and subtracted: GB/s is size * reps over the kernel time (BS-3). The buffer starts on a 64-byte boundary in the c, rust, zig and go columns (BS-4); the mk column's is an arena slice (labelled alignment exception, below).

mk: the width-fixed cells (review finding BF-1, B16), indexbyte.c's loop with Vec[u8, L], Mask.Any and Mask.FirstSet, no run-time dispatch, L chosen per package as mandelvec does: mkfixv2/ (L = 16, one xmm) in the v2 variants, mkfix/ (L = 32, one ymm) in the v3 variants. Every variant's quick and publish checksum was checked with the row's own mk line, untimed, by M9 item 11.7 (2026-11-15, mk built from ca6060e8; plan/09-deferred.md). mk/ is the std-simd lane's program (std.simd.IndexByte, which picks its form at run time, D-353) and is no cell of this table.

The Mk cells are labelled alignment exception: the Mk buffer is an arena slice, and Mk code cannot read or set an address without std.raw (banned in every table, BS-8) (status/std-simd.md R-5 (a)). But std's heap arenas start a slice of 4 KiB or more on a cache line, and a probe (2026-11-19, a scratch package with std.raw) finds the slice at 0 mod 64 at 16 KiB, 32 MiB and 1 GiB; TestArenaOffsetsAsLabelled rebuilds that probe with the tree's mk. Their loads do not align themselves, and need not: at v3 none of the 32-byte loads cross a cache line and at v2 none of the 16-byte loads does, as in the 64-byte-aligned columns.
